_README: The manifest that decides what news matters. YAAIN's filter reads THIS, not a hardcoded prompt. If you install something on brownie or the studio, or pin/upgrade a tool, UPDATE THIS FILE IN THE SAME BREATH — otherwise YAAIN decays into exactly the staleness it exists to prevent. Last audited against the machines: 2026-08-30 (refs/yaain-landscape-review-2026-08-30.md part (a)). AND WHEN YOU ADD A MODEL, WRITE ITS `chosen` BLOCK IN THE SAME COMMIT — the reason, the date, and a pointer to the entry that records it. A model with no recorded reason is one nobody can supersede on purpose later; if there genuinely was no decision, say so.

machines.name: studio
machines.role: local text inference for the whole fleet
machines.ceiling: ~96GB wired practical; ~100GB observed stall point. The real constraint is reading speed (~180 tok/s), not memory.

machines.name: brownie
machines.hardware: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti, 16GB VRAM, 64GB RAM, Windows 11, Blackwell sm_120
machines.ceiling: 16GB VRAM is a HARD WALL. A model needing 24GB is unusable to us at any price. Python 3.13.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130 — an ABI mismatch is real breakage, not a detail.

models.name: qwen3.6
models.detail: 27b-bf16 / 27b-coding-bf16 / 27b-q8_0 / 27b-q4_K_M / 35b-a3b MoE. `bosun-brain` is the q4_K_M at 98,304 ctx, ~23.6GB resident.
models.used_by: Bosun's own brain; repo-hunter enrich+explain; mac-hunter llm_generic; takomagether social drafts + council attribution

chosen.why: Bosun's brain, set in the Hermes phase-1 build: the largest model the studio already served that still leaves room for co-tenants, and off-API per the local-first preference. RECORDED AS PROVISIONAL AT THE TIME — a brain bake-off was planned and has still never run (it was waiting on the council batch to release the studio; that finished 2026-08-21, so it is unblocked).
chosen.revisit_if: the bake-off runs, OR a newer Qwen generation clears the same four bars — Apache-2.0, ungated, ~27B class, served by Ollama. Qwen3.8-27B meets all four as of 2026-08-30 and this decision was never finalised, so it is the weakest of our model choices, not the strongest.

chosen.why: The Apache-2.0 default for image generation in the render-PC plan, which treated licensing as a hard spec rather than a preference. The traps it was chosen against were the popular ones — FLUX.1 [dev] and FLUX.2 klein are non-commercial.
chosen.revisit_if: a successor at a licence at least as clean that still fits 16GB

models.name: Hunyuan3D 2.0
models.detail: DiT v2.0, shape + texture. LICENCE UNRESOLVED: Tencent Community licence excludes the EU/UK/South Korea including the OUTPUT — awaiting Em's ruling.

chosen.why: Installed and proven end to end (shape AND texture) the same night. LICENCE UNRESOLVED AND IT IS EM'S CALL: the Tencent Community licence permits commercial use under 1M MAU but territorially excludes the EU, UK and South Korea, and extends that to the OUTPUT — i.e. you may not display results there. That is the same shape as the MiniMax H3 licence a model was deleted over the same day, and a public website is displayed in the UK/EU by definition.
chosen.revisit_if: Em rules on the territorial licence, OR a licence-clean successor appears. NOTE: tencent/Hy4-preview is NOT that successor — it is a 780B text model. Tencent's real 3D line is Hunyuan3D-2.1, published 2025-06-13, i.e. older than this choice.

models.name: TRELLIS.2 (trellis.cpp)
models.detail: trellis.cpp v0.6.0 (installed 2026-08-29), MIT, standalone C++/GGML, no Python/torch — so it cannot disturb ComfyUI. We run the f16 weights (~16.5GB); q8 (~9.5GB) and q4 (~6GB) exist since v0.5.4 via the installer's --quant flag and would sit well under the 16GB VRAM wall. The Python wrapper route is DEAD on our torch 2.13 ABI.

chosen.why: Chosen as the LICENCE-CLEAN image-to-3D path, deliberately alongside Hunyuan3D rather than instead of it: MIT end to end (trellis.cpp, TRELLIS.2-4B, BiRefNet), and it uses ungated mirrors so it needs no DINOv3 licence click. A standalone C++/GGML binary with no Python or torch, so it cannot disturb the ComfyUI install — which is also why it sidesteps the torch-ABI wall that killed the Python wrapper route.
chosen.revisit_if: quality proves inadequate against Hunyuan3D, or the Hunyuan3D licence is ruled clean. Quality caveat softened 2026-08-30: the maintainer measured statistical parity with the reference pipeline at v0.4.3 (multi-seed, matched-conditioning A/B), but CUDA geometry then regressed at v0.5.4 and was fixed at v0.6.0 with no restated parity measurement, so parity is claimed for a build one regression-and-fix behind ours. Our own evidence on v0.6.0 is Em's by-sight approval of the pipe-holder render (2026-08-30), not a measurement.

models.name: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
models.detail: Apache-2.0, 16.6GB, one-shot by design (a resident critic would pin ~16GB on our only render tier)
models.used_by: the video judge; NDN's design critic

chosen.why: Chosen for the vision tier because licence is a hard spec: Apache-2.0 and ungated, verified against BOTH the model card and the HF API rather than one page-read. Picked over Gemma 3, which is gated and use-restricted — the same class of problem that got MiniMax H3 deleted the day before. It also installs nothing, running on the Python/torch/transformers already on brownie.
chosen.revisit_if: a replacement is proposed — re-run the discriminating two-image test in brownie/README.md first. 'It described something reasonable' is not a pass; the failure mode being guarded against is a model that answers fluently about a picture it never saw.

models.name: gemma-3-12b
models.detail: gemma-3-12b-it + mmproj, the LTX-2 text encoder

chosen.why: NOT A CHOICE — it arrived as LTX-2.3's required text encoder and is on disk because LTX-2.3 is. Its own vision weights are unusable to us (the GGUF mmproj is transposed by ComfyUI-GGUF), which is part of why the vision tier is a separate model.
chosen.revisit_if: LTX is replaced or upgraded — this follows whatever LTX needs

constraints: VRAM <= 16GB on brownie. This is the single most important filter on relevance — most model announcements are written for 24-80GB cards. A quantisation that brings a model under 16GB is itself the news.

LICENCE IS A HARD SPEC, NOT A PREFERENCE. Apache-2.0 and MIT are the defaults. TERRITORIAL RESTRICTIONS ARE DISQUALIFYING - MiniMax H3 was deleted over exactly this (2026-08-29), and Hunyuan3D 2.0's territorial exclusion of the EU/UK/South Korea is still awaiting a ruling. A gated model costs a human licence click.
Blackwell sm_120 compatibility on brownie is real breakage, not a footnote.
brownie runs Python 3.13.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130. Wheels built for another torch do not load.
Off-API preference: local first, metered only where metering is the point.
Loader dependencies matter as much as models (LTX-2.3 loads through UnetLoaderGGUF, not UNETLoader).

licence_policy.disqualifying: any territorial restriction on use OR on the output; any non-commercial clause
licence_policy.needs_human: gated models (a licence click), and any bespoke community licence

_CHOSEN: Every model carries a dated `chosen` block: WHY we picked it, WHEN, a pointer to the dated entry that is the real record, and where known what would supersede it. The point is that when something newer appears we can weigh it against the reason rather than just mute it. Where no decision was ever recorded the block SAYS SO rather than inventing one. The `ref` is a pointer, never a restatement — the journal entry is the source of record.

retired.name: MiniMax H3
retired.why: DELETED, Em's call, on licence: the MiniMax H3 Community Licence carries territorial and commercial-use restrictions, which makes it unusable for a publication. 39.56GB reclaimed across four files; it had never been run, and LTX-2 also does joint audio+video, which was its distinguishing feature. Recorded because it is the strongest precedent we have for licence-as-a-hard-spec — and so a successor is not proposed without reading its licence first.
